key_insight: Treat scaling-law estimation as a budget-aware sequential experimental-design problem: actively pick pilot runs based on cost and informativeness to fit scaling laws more accurately for less money.
problem_solved: Pilot experiments used to fit scaling laws are themselves costly and heterogeneous in compute price; naive or uniform sampling wastes budget and can produce poor extrapolations for planning large-scale runs.
method: Formulate scaling-law fitting as budget-aware sequential experiment selection from a finite pool of runnable configurations with heterogeneous costs.
Use an acquisition strategy that trades off expected information gain (or uncertainty reduction) against run cost to prioritize experiments with high value per dollar.
Iteratively run selected experiments, update the scaling-law fit, and re-select under the remaining budget until budget is exhausted or fit converges.
impact: Enables practitioners to obtain reliable scaling-law fits with substantially lower pilot cost, improving resource allocation and more trustworthy planning of expensive large-scale training runs.
visual_elements: Budget vs. fit accuracy curve showing active selection reaching target accuracy at lower cost than uniform sampling
Flowchart of the sequential loop: candidate pool -> cost/informativeness scoring -> run selection -> model update -> repeat
Scatter plot of candidate experiments (e.g., model size × data) with selected runs highlighted to show coverage and cost-efficiency
Icon set: wallet/coin (budget), magnifying glass (informativeness), clock/server (compute cost)
paper_title: Spend Less, Fit Better: Budget-Efficient Scaling Law Fitting via Active Experiment Selection
paper_authors: Sijie Li, Shanda Li, Haowei Lin, Weiwei Sun, Ameet Talwalkar
